metadata.title: South Korea’s Lee urges faster AI investment during $5.2bn data center visit

content.text:
Investing.com -- South Korean President Lee Jae Myung called for faster investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure Saturday during a visit to a $5.2 billion data center project being developed by SK Group and Amazon Web Services.
Lee toured the construction site in Ulsan, southeastern South Korea, highlighting growing competition among countries seeking to attract investment in AI computing capacity.
The president stressed the need to accelerate infrastructure development as governments and technology companies race to expand their artificial intelligence capabilities.
The Ulsan facility is being developed jointly by SK Group, South Korea's second-largest conglomerate, and Amazon Web Services, the cloud computing division of Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN).
The project is expected to require approximately 7 trillion won ($5.2 billion) in investment through 2029, according to estimates released by South Korea's science ministry last year.
Initial operations are scheduled to begin in the second half of 2027.
SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won previously outlined plans to develop 103 megawatts of computing capacity by 2029, with the potential to add nearly 900 megawatts in subsequent expansion phases.
The conglomerate is seeking further partnerships with international technology companies as construction progresses.
Lee expressed hopes that the facility would attract additional global AI investment and strengthen South Korea's position in the expanding data center industry.
The project could also support demand for advanced semiconductors, an industry central to South Korea's technology exports.
Lee highlighted the facility's location outside the Seoul metropolitan area, where much of the country's AI investment has traditionally been concentrated.
He described the Ulsan development as an example of how major technology projects could support regional economic growth.
Workforce availability also emerged as a concern during the visit.
After learning that approximately 900 workers were employed at the construction site, Lee called on government ministries to examine training programs for workers needed to build data centers and related AI infrastructure.
